messages:
alex: heads up — canary nodes in eu-west-1 are showing a steady mem growth after the 5421 rollout, looks like OOMs on longctx workloads. initial spike around 11:03 UTC.
maya: saw the alerts, thanks. any obvious GC churn or mutex logs?
alex: no, GC looks normal. attaching quick `smem -k` snapshot I grabbed: total RSS per process jumped from 6.2g -> 18.9g over ~8 minutes for `redwood-runtime`.
jordan: curious if this is fragmentation vs allocations. can you run `pmap -x` + `curl /debug/heap` for the failing pod?
alex: pasted heap dump to /tmp/heap-1871234567.txt (short snippet below):
```
# heap profile top 20
226M  40%  hashmap.resize
120M  21%  kv::entry::payload
45M   8%   batched_request::buffers
... rest small
```
alex: `hashmap.resize` stands out — looks like a rehash/resize cascade. we batch small requests so there might be many tiny maps being promoted under load.
dicego: quick note — PR 5421 changed `KvMap::grow_factor` from 1.5 -> 2.0 to reduce rehash frequency. it also switched to power-of-two resizing and deferred allocations in the hot path. I thought it reduced churn but maybe allocation pattern interacts with the arena.
maya: can you `kubectl exec` and run `pprof --alloc_objects` to get stack traces?
jordan: I ran `pprof` on one canary pod; sample stack traces point to `KvMap::insert -> maybe_rehash -> allocate_new_buckets` and then `arena_alloc` calls. grafting a snippet: `kv_map.rs:412 kv_map::resize -> alloc::vec::Vec::reserve -> jemalloc`
diego: interesting — earlier we saw fragmentation after switching allocator knobs in 5408. combination might be the issue. 5421 reduces rehash frequency but the resize amplifies when it does happen.
tasha: CI also flagged a small perf regression in the nightly throughput tests — around 4.8% drop for longctx workloads after 5421 merged (bench logs in CI job 2026-03-16-rt-longctx). could be related.
alex: I'm going to roll 5421 out of canary (revert) and see if memory stabilizes. tagging @diego for context.
sre-bot: deploy revert started: rolling back deployment redwood-runtime:5421 -> 5419 to namespace prod-canary-eu-west-1
maya: after revert, memory flattened within two minutes on the pod we watched. no further OOMs in the canary group for the last 20m.
jordan: that pretty strongly implicates 5421. can we reproduce locally with a stress harness that mimics batching pattern? If so we should add a regression test.
diego: agreed. I can repro in a microbenchmark: with 16 concurrent clients doing variable sequence-length requests (mix of short/long), the map resize triggers when one big request blows up a map and causes bucket growth. Also saw `malloc` spikes in `strace`. I'll open a minimal repro repo.
maya: can we land a hotfix that caps max bucket growth during warmup and defers rehash to background thread? maybe restrict growth factor to 1.25 for under-60s age maps.
diego: working on a patch: `kv: cap_growth_during_hotpath` — will add metrics (`kv.rehash_sync_count`) and a histogram for bucket_size. will also add a unit test that simulates 10k small maps and triggers concurrent resize.
jordan: file INF-3219 for tracking, assign to diego. include bench artifacts and heap profiles.
alex: thanks — for now reverting was the right call. let's also add CI perf check against longctx nightly to catch throughput regressions before rollout.
maya: noted. I'll add a gating step in rollout pipeline that compares mem/throughput to baseline for canary.
sre-bot: ticket INF-3219 created and assigned to diego.
alex: OK closing thread after smaller follow-ups. feel free to continue updates here or open PR review comments. :thumbsup:
